source.quote: Cambridge Audio's own page for the Evo 150 SE, read 2026-11-24. Row « COMPATIBILITY »: « TOSLINK optical: 16/24bit 32-96kHz PCM only S/PDIF coaxial: 16/24bit 32-192kHz PCM only », « USB Audio Class 1: Up to 24-bit 96kHz (asynchronous) USB Audio Class 2: Up to 24-bit 384kHz (asynchronous) and up to DSD 256 », « Bluetooth: 4.2 A2DP/ AVRCP supporting up to aptX HD (24bit 48kHz) », « ARC: 16/24bit 32-192kHz PCM only ». DAC row: « ESS Sabre ES9018K2M ». No filter or oversampling row.

facts.chip: « ESS Sabre ES9018K2M » (ESS), from the page's DAC row.

_PCM_only_dit_explicitement_quil_ny_a_pa: « 16/24bit 32-96kHz PCM only » on optical, « 32-192kHz PCM only » on coaxial and on ARC. The word « only » is the maker closing the DSD question for three inputs - and inputs.dsd_max has no value for « none », exactly the gap the Schiit Yggdrasil opened an hour earlier. Three more inputs that need the word, on a second maker. The field is left absent on them, which reads as « nobody asked » when the page answers.
_les_deux_classes_usb_encore_et_un_ecart: « USB Audio Class 1: Up to 24-bit 96kHz » against « USB Audio Class 2: Up to 24-bit 384kHz and up to DSD 256 ». Same shape as the Evo 300, factor of four instead of eight, and DSD available in Class 2 only. Two models of one maker publishing it makes the USB-class split a documented pattern rather than a curiosity.
